```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Chunk 1: Package Imports
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r load_data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Chunk 2: Load and Organize Data
file_path <- "CorticalVolume_EEG_correlation.xlsx"
data <- read_excel(file_path, na = c("", "NA", "N/A", "n/a", "nan", "NaN"))

cat("Master dataset loaded successfully.\n")
cat(sprintf("Total Animals: %d | Total Columns: %d\n", nrow(data), ncol(data)))
cat("Variables available for correlation:\n")
print(names(data)[3:ncol(data)])
```

```{r correlation_function, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Chunk 3: Pairwise Correlation and Plotting Function
run_pairwise_correlations <- function(data, 
                                     colors = c("Sham" = "#0099FF", 
                                                "Sham + CSD" = "#005698", 
                                                "TBI" = "#FF7474", 
                                                "TBI + CSD" = "#A20000"),
                                     method = c("pearson", "spearman"),
                                     show_se = TRUE,
                                     point_size = 3.0,
                                     aspect_ratio = 1.1,
                                     save = "all",
                                     save_format = c("svg", "png", "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff"),
                                     save_dpi = 300,
                                     save_width = 6,
                                     save_height = 5) {
  
  method <- match.arg(method)
  save_format <- match.arg(save_format)
  
  # Select all analysis columns (excluding Animal and Group)
  numeric_cols <- names(data)[3:ncol(data)]
  
  if (length(numeric_cols) < 2) {
    stop("Need at least 2 numeric feature columns to calculate pairwise correlations.")
  }
  
  # Generate unique pairwise combinations
  pair_combos <- combn(numeric_cols, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("Generated %d unique pairwise comparisons.\n\n", length(pair_combos)))
  
  # Resolve which plot indices to save
  total_combos <- length(pair_combos)
  save_indices <- if (identical(save, "all")) {
    seq_len(total_combos)
  } else if (is.numeric(save)) {
    intersect(save, seq_len(total_combos))
  } else {
    integer(0)
  }
  
  plots_list <- list()
  results_list <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_along(pair_combos)) {
    var_x <- pair_combos[[i]][1]
    var_y <- pair_combos[[i]][2]
    
    # Pairwise complete-case filtering (only drop NA for this specific pair)
    pair_df <- data %>%
      select(Animal_id, Group, all_of(var_x), all_of(var_y)) %>%
      filter(!is.na(.data[[var_x]]) & !is.na(.data[[var_y]])) %>%
      droplevels()
    
    n_complete <- nrow(pair_df)
    
    # Guard clause if insufficient data points exist
    if (n_complete < 3) {
      cat(sprintf("Skipping %s vs %s: fewer than 3 complete cases (n = %d).\n", var_x, var_y, n_complete))
      next
    }
    
    # Run statistical test across all animals combined
    cor_test <- cor.test(pair_df[[var_x]], pair_df[[var_y]], method = method)
    r_val <- cor_test$estimate
    p_val <- cor_test$p.value
    
    # Format labels for Prism-like annotation
    stat_symbol <- if (method == "pearson") "italic(R)^2" else "italic(r)[s]"
    stat_label <- sprintf("%s == %.3f * ',' ~ italic(p) == %.4f * ',' ~ italic(n) == %d", 
                          stat_symbol, r_val^2, p_val, n_complete)
    
    # Record statistical summary
    results_list[[paste0(var_x, "_vs_", var_y)]] <- data.frame(
      Index = i,
      Variable_X = var_x,
      Variable_Y = var_y,
      N = n_complete,
      Correlation = round(unname(r_val), 4),
      p_value = round(p_val, 5),
      Method = tools::toTitleCase(method),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Generate standalone scatter plot
    p <- ggplot(pair_df, aes(x = .data[[var_x]], y = .data[[var_y]])) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = "black", linewidth = 1.0, se = show_se, alpha = 0.15) +
      geom_point(aes(fill = Group), shape = 21, size = point_size, stroke = 0.9, color = "black", alpha = 0.9) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
      theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
      labs(
        title = sprintf("%s vs. %s", var_x, var_y),
        subtitle = parse(text = stat_label),
        x = var_x,
        y = var_y
      ) +
      theme(
        aspect.ratio = aspect_ratio,
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, color = "black"),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1.0),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1.0),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
      )
    
    print(p)
    plots_list[[paste0(var_x, "_vs_", var_y)]] <- p
    
    # Save file if this index is selected
    if (i %in% save_indices) {
      file_name <- sprintf("cor_%02d_%s_vs_%s.%s", i, var_x, var_y, save_format)
      ggsave(
        filename = file_name, 
        plot = p, 
        width = save_width, 
        height = save_height, 
        device = save_format,
        dpi = save_dpi
      )
      cat(sprintf("  -> Saved %s: %s\n", toupper(save_format), file_name))
    }
  }
  
  summary_table <- bind_rows(results_list)
  cat("\n=======================================================\n")
  cat("CORRELATION SUMMARY TABLE\n")
  cat("=======================================================\n")
  print(summary_table)
  
  return(invisible(list(
    summary = summary_table,
    plots = plots_list
  )))
}
```

```{r run_analysis, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.8}
# Chunk 4: Execute Pairwise Correlations
correlation_output <- run_pairwise_correlations(
  data = data,
  method = "pearson",  # Change to "spearman" if rank correlations are preferred
  point_size = 3.2,
  aspect_ratio = 1.1,
  show_se = TRUE,
  save = NULL,
  save_format = "jpeg"
)
```
